holidays.name: National Seafood Bisque Day
holidays.description: A day to treat yourself to a velvety, spoon-coating bowl of creamy shellfish soup. Lobster, crab, shrimp, or crawfish all qualify, so long as the result is silky and rich.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It is celebrated every year on October 19, during National Seafood Month.
holidays.funFact: Bisque was traditionally thickened with rice and made from crushed shellfish shells. That is why the best versions taste so deeply of the sea.

holidays.name: Evaluate Your Life Day
holidays.description: A day to pause, take stock of where you are, and decide whether your goals, habits, and choices still fit you. Think of it as a mini performance review, with you as both boss and employee.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed every year on October 19.
holidays.funFact: Fall is a popular time for taking stock. The year's final quarter is close enough that you can still act on what you decide.

holidays.name: International Gin and Tonic Day
holidays.description: A toast to the fizzy, bitter-sweet, lime-garnished highball. It is a day to raise a glass of gin and tonic water over plenty of ice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and the exact origin is unclear. It is listed on October 19 in holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Tonic water gets its bitter edge from quinine. British colonial officials in India once used quinine to fight malaria, and mixing it with gin made it easier to drink.
